report.title: NO at CIN Week 12 Scouting Report: Saints at Bengals
report.summary: Cincinnati is a heavy early-down passer that can stall on early-down runs, so New Orleans should force it to throw from behind schedule. The Bengals' blitz is modest, but their third-down defense is vulnerable, and injuries have thinned the Saints' interior line. Special teams and field position could decide a close game.

sections.heading: Opponent offense
sections.body: Cincinnati drops back on 61.9% of first downs [oc1] over 278 plays [oc2] and on 81.0% of third downs [oc5] over 116 plays [oc6], so expect obvious passing situations. Targets concentrate on J.Chase at 25.9% [oc9] and T.Higgins at 20.5% [oc10]. The passing game is mostly short, with an average depth of target of 7.2 yards [oc12] over 378 attempts [oc13], though its explosive pass rate is 8.6% [oc14] over 408 pass plays [oc15]. The run game is inefficient, with EPA of -0.06 per run [oc19] over 194 runs [oc20]. Third-down conversion of 50.0% [oc22] ranks 2nd in the league [oc23], so keep the offense off schedule and keep Chase and Higgins in front of the defense.

sections.heading: Opponent defense
sections.body: Cincinnati blitzes on 15.2% of dropbacks [dc1] over 389 plays [dc2], but its pressure proxy of 14.9% [dc3] ranks only 17th [dc4]. Its passing downs are where its rushers can cash in. The defense allows explosive pass plays on 9.5% of attempts [dc6] and explosive runs on 10.6% of runs [dc8]. Third down is the soft spot: opponents convert 44.4% [dc12] over 124 plays [dc13], ranking 25th [dc14]. Overall success allowed is 45.8% [dc18], ranking 24th [dc19]. With 5.8 defenders in the box on runs [dc10] and 5.5 on passes [dc11], play action and quick-game concepts can exploit the lighter fronts, but the Saints must stay on schedule on first and second down.

sections.heading: Special teams
sections.body: McPherson has made 15 [kc1] of 16 [kc2] field goal tries and is 100.0% [kc3] from 50-plus on 7 [kc4] attempts, so trust him on long kicks. Carlson made 8 [kc5] of 12 [kc6] for New Orleans before his last game, and C.Smyth has made 6 [kc7] of 8 [kc8] in recent weeks. Cincinnati's punts net 42.0 yards [kc9], against a 38.8-yard net [kc12] for New Orleans, so expect the Bengals to win the field-position battle. Kick away from the returner only when the return is the bigger threat.

sections.heading: Injuries and availability
sections.body: Cincinnati's latest report lists G Dalton Risner as Out [ic2] with a knee injury; he has played in 9 games [ic4], so expect a backup at guard. WR Andrei Iosivas is Doubtful [ic5] and LB Oren Burks is Out [ic8]. New Orleans lists C Erik McCoy as Out [ic13] and T Taliese Fuaga as Out [ic16], so the interior and tackle spots need reshuffling. Chris Olave takes 27.8% of targets [ic19] over 367 team targets [ic20].

sections.heading: Key matchups
sections.body: Pass protection is the first concern. Cincinnati sends five or more rushers on 15.2% of dropbacks [mc1]. With C Erik McCoy out after a 96.5% snap share [mc4] over 8 games [mc5] and T Taliese Fuaga out after 100.0% of snaps [mc6] over 8 games [mc7], keep a back or tight end in on interior fronts. Third down is the second matchup: Cincinnati converts 50.0% of its third downs [mc8], but its defense allows 44.4% [mc10] over 124 plays [mc11], so Chris Olave's 27.8% target share [mc13] should work on crossers and option routes. The third matchup is Chase and Higgins, at 25.9% [mc14] and 20.5% [mc15] of targets, against light boxes, where play action works but safety help must be set over the top. Finally, Cincinnati's punt net of 42.0 yards [mc19] beats New Orleans' 38.8 yards [mc20], and McPherson has made 15 [mc21] of 16 [mc22] field goals, so the Saints must win the yardage battle.
